figure-title.purpose: A figure's title, its chapter's own: 300 at 2.75rem (--text-2xl), line height 1.1, -0.01em, text-wrap balance.

figure-title-phone.purpose: The figure's title below 45rem: 2rem (--text-2xl-phone), so the server's basin reaches a phone's first screen.

title.purpose: Light titles: the basin dialog's title.

caption.purpose: A figure's live caption and the list's empty state; 38ch, text-wrap pretty, in --text-2.

body.purpose: Row names and field text; the base set on body.

body-strong.purpose: Emphasis inside a line: a row's amount, a band's state word, a rejected item's name.

body-sm.purpose: Status line, band sentence, rejection reason, dialog note, part tabs, a quick add's hint, a figure's "Preparing the world…".

note.purpose: A few words beside a code block's path: the reference panel's "Not running in this figure". The words of a choice (Then, Now) and Then's date take the same face and size, set solid (line height 1).

name.purpose: The app's name in the masthead only; uppercase, tracked 0.32em.

label.purpose: Button labels, category heads and a choice's legend (Speed, Version); uppercase, tracked 0.18em.

label-lg.purpose: A device's name over its pane in a figure, and a code block's title; uppercase, tracked 0.18em.

mono.purpose: Ids, versions, counts, file paths and the short state lines built on them: #15, v9 · synced, Add #15, 2 left, beat 2 of 4 · 5.00 s, a code block's path (src/lib/sync.ts, --text-3) and note (A · #6), Then's commit. Set solid (line height 1) for a speed option, a message's label on a wire and a basin's version label.

mono-mark.purpose: The device mark: the first four characters of the client id.

code.purpose: Every line of code: Spline Sans Mono 400 at 0.8125rem (--text-code), line height 1.6, tab size 2, at a size whose longest engine lines fit a figure's code column. No line numbers, no gutter. Colours from the --code-* aliases.

shadows.name: basin-inset
shadows.value: inset 0 2px 8px light-dark(rgb(10 26 51 / 0.12), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55)), inset 0 0 0 var(--rule) var(--line)
shadows.purpose: Recessed water: every basin, on an ::after overlay because the canvas would paint over an inset shadow on the box. Dropped under forced colours for a 1px CanvasText edge.

shadows.name: dock
shadows.purpose: The add form while docked at the foot of a phone; none from 45rem.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: The dialog's ::backdrop background (a colour, not a box-shadow).

motion.name: motion-state
motion.purpose: Colour and edge changes on buttons, fields, the check, tabs, the remove control, the badge's frame and a choice's options.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The easing for every CSS state transition.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: A basin change settling into the water: SETTLE_MS in src/ui/marbling/mount.ts, --settle in tokens.css.

motion.name: settle-ease
motion.purpose: The basin's exponential ease-out (easeOut in src/ui/marbling/operations.ts): quick to land, slow to still.

motion.name: strip-fade
motion.purpose: The outbox strip's trailing fade where changes run past the edge, driven by animation-timeline: scroll(self inline).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every CSS animation and transition; basins show changes at once, as the CPU path always does.

motion.name: figure-settle
motion.purpose: A figure's basins settle only while its world plays (the scene, free play, a reader's change); a jump (scrub, Back, Step, Restart, a fork, Play from the end) shows its instant at once.

motion.name: message-travel
motion.purpose: A message travels its lane, beside its straight wire and stopping 12 px above the device's pane, as the world's clock runs (distance is time). Reduced motion, read once and followed as it changes: it sits at its sender's end of the lane for the first half of its flight and at its receiver's for the second.

motion.name: lost-fade
motion.purpose: A lost message's "… · lost" label fades out where it was dropped (LOST_MARK_MILLIS in src/lib/sandbox/frame.ts).

motion.name: lit-settle
motion.purpose: A newly lit span of code settles in: its --ink-2 rule and --water wash rise from transparent. A jump (scrub, Back, Step, Restart, a fork, Play from the end) and reduced motion show it at once.

motion.name: code-scroll
motion.purpose: Lit lines outside the code's view scroll into it a third of the way down, snapped to the start of a whole line (the block's line height from its top padding). Only the code's own box scrolls (scrollTo), never the page.

motion.name: then-now-morph
motion.purpose: Then and Now from a 40rem panel: @shikijs/magic-move moves matching tokens and fades the rest out or in, at --settle's length on --ease-out's curve. Reduced motion replaces at once; below a 40rem panel the choice cuts between per-line drawings.

breakpoints.name: form-inline
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport min-width: the add form leaves the foot dock and becomes the first row under the masthead.

breakpoints.name: list-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Container min-width on the list: the remove control becomes word and cross (6rem).

breakpoints.name: figure-phone
breakpoints.purpose: A figure's phone composition: a 2rem title, a 1rem row gap, playback's four buttons on one row, the devices a swipeable strip of min(85%, 22rem).

breakpoints.name: figure-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport min-width: words and controls in the left third, the stage in the right two thirds; speed and Your turn under playback instead of under the stage. A figure with code puts its code in a full-width row under both columns until 80rem.

breakpoints.name: stage-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Container min-width on the stage (`container: stage / inline-size`): the server's compact list beside its basin, the basin at least 23rem. On a narrower stage, whatever the viewport, the list sits above a full-width basin.

breakpoints.name: figure-code-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport min-width, a figure with code only (Stage | code, the user's choice of 2026-10-17): a band of copy and playback across the top, then the stage at minmax(47rem, 3fr) beside a sticky code column at minmax(0, 2fr), held to 100dvh less 1.5rem above and below; speed, Your turn and the breaking controls under the stage.

breakpoints.name: playback-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Playback's cell in the Stage | code band: its four buttons keep one row, flex 1 1 0, none narrower than its label, as on a phone.

breakpoints.name: then-and-now-wide
breakpoints.purpose: Then and Now's panel: from 40rem the magic-move morph shows and Then's date sits beside it on one line; narrower, per-line code with hanging indents, a cut between versions, and Then's date under it.

basin.featherScaling: FEATHER_CSS_PX * min(1, width / 320)^2, so a 92px badge keeps its ink
basin.dropsPerItem: five drops (ink, clear, ring, clear, core) and a laying stroke; a checked item adds a stroke across
basin.order: confirmed items by server version (ties by id), then outbox items in fresh ink in this device's order
basin.renderers: one shared WebGL2 context (16 samples still, 4 while settling, up to 1.5 device px); CPU fallback at half the box, one sample a pixel, never settles

scale.figure: scaleFor(mostRows(timeline)): items cover about 27% of the water (FILL 0.27), clamped to 1..1.75 (MAX_SCALE); fixed for the figure's life

versionLabels.text: v{version}, Mono 0.75rem / 1 in --text-2 on a 3px --water text-shadow halo
versionLabels.box: 26 x 14 CSS px, 4px (--space-1) off its drop's outer ring
versionLabels.placement: just outside the outer ring on clear water: sides then corners, stepping out 0.04 world units up to 8 steps where rings press together; clearest spot wins; newest placed first, older labels give way; never overlapping

grid.narrow: one column: copy, playback, stage, pace, breaking; gap 1.5rem (1rem below 45rem)
grid.wide: from 64rem: minmax(18rem, 1fr) minmax(0, 2fr), column gap 3rem; copy, playback, pace, breaking on the left, the stage spanning on the right

withCode.narrow: below 64rem: copy, playback, stage, pace, breaking, code
withCode.medium: 64rem to 80rem: the two columns as without code, then the code in a full-width row
withCode.wide: from 80rem: columns minmax(47rem, 3fr) minmax(0, 2fr), column gap 3rem; areas "copy playback" "stage code" "pace code" "breaking code"; playback aligned to the band's foot
withCode.stickyCode: position sticky, top 1.5rem (--space-5), max-block-size calc(100dvh - 2 * --space-5); the code scrolls inside it
withCode.stageFloor: 47rem, the server row's container threshold, so the server keeps its list beside its basin and A, B and C stay in the first view

stage.order: server row, wire band, device row
stage.serverRowWide: from a 47rem stage (container query): basin minmax(0, 1fr), at least 23rem, list 22rem (two compact 10rem columns), gap 2rem, top-aligned
stage.serverRowNarrow: below a 47rem stage, whatever the viewport: list above a full-width basin
stage.deviceRow: grid-auto-flow column, minmax(14rem, 1fr), gap 2rem, overflow-x auto, scroll-snap x mandatory

wireBand.wire: 1px --line, straight, from the band's top (the lower of the server basin's foot and its list's) across the basin's span to the device pane's top above its middle; each message's lane stops deviceInsetPx above the pane (label half-height 7 + halo 3 + gap 2), lane offset included, so no message, held message or lost mark sits on the pane's header
wireBand.held: no fill, --text-2 stroke, dasharray 2 2, label "… · held"
wireBand.lost: label only, "… · lost" in --text-3, fading over 600ms of world time

density.compactList: groups 1rem apart, heads 0.25rem over rows; with columns={2} (the server's list only) columns: 10rem 2, column gap 1.5rem, a group never split
density.deviceList: compact while a scene plays, regular in free play; one column at any width

code.font: Spline Sans Mono Variable 400, 0.8125rem (--text-code), line height 1.6, tab size 2; no line numbers
code.highlighting: build time only (src/build/highlight.ts, Shiki's CSS-variables theme with prefix --code-); no highlighter in the page
code.block: head (title, path, then a note or the reference note), 0.75rem gap, then the code under a 1px --line rule, padding-block 0.75rem, overflow auto, tabindex 0; no card
code.wrap: white-space pre-wrap, overflow-wrap anywhere; each line padding-inline-start calc(--space-3 + --indent + 2ch - --lit-rule) with text-indent -(--indent + 2ch), padding-inline-end --space-3; --indent is the line's leading spaces in ch
code.edge: text --space-3 in from the head and the rule in every block, lit or not; the lit rule's 1px comes out of the line's inset (--lit-rule)

lit.rule: the latest trace event at or before the playhead that a light answers lights that light's span, until another does; the first light wins a tie; nothing before any
lit.element: <mark>, display block, background --water, border-inline-start 1px (--rule) solid --ink-2, color inherit
lit.settle: animation from transparent rule and wash over --settle with --ease-out, only while the world plays and motion is allowed
lit.note: at the head's far end, Mono --text-2: whose code ran and on what (A · #6, A · ack #5, poke v7)
lit.forcedColors: the system's mark colours; the rule, a border, stays

code.reference: running={false}: "Not running in this figure" in Note type --text-2 after the path; never lit, no note

thenAndNow.choice: Version: Then (date in Commissioner --text-3, commit in Mono) and Now
thenAndNow.wide: from a 40rem panel: magic-move morph, 900ms, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); wraps flush on the shared edge (no hanging indent); Then's date on one line beside it
thenAndNow.narrow: below a 40rem panel: per-line drawing with hanging indents, a cut between versions; Then's date and commit under "Then", start-aligned; Now one line, centred
thenAndNow.hidden: the other drawing is display none, so the code is never read twice
thenAndNow.firstPaint: Then from build-time HTML, before any script runs

narrative.overview:
One ink family on still water. Every colour but one is a dilution of the same indigo: indigo depth on paper-white water by day, mist on indigo water at night, with ink current, dilute ink and feathered grey between them. The single second hue is a vermilion seal, pressed only where a change was rejected or sync stopped. Day and night are each designed, both follow the system's setting, and any subtree can pin one (`data-theme="day"` or `"night"`).

The list leads. Words, rows and controls sit on a still margin divided by 1 px hairlines, with no cards and no fills behind rows, set in a quiet humanist sans whose weight axis carries the hierarchy and a soft mono for every id and count. Density is a working phone list: 46 px rows, 44 px targets, one 45rem column on a desktop. Code is the engine's own source on the same margin, under a hairline and never in a card: one ink in tonal steps, wrapping at its measure, with the branch a figure's world last ran washed in water.

The signature is the basin: recessed water in which each device marbles its own list with exact, area-preserving marbling math. It is computed from the rows the device holds, never simulated and never random, so devices that agree show the same pattern line for line and a device that is behind visibly differs. In the app it is a 92 px badge beside the name that opens full size; in a figure the server's basin heads the stage, a straight hairline wire runs from under it to every device, and each device's basin heads its pane. Every change settles into the water over 900 ms (in a figure, only while its world plays); otherwise the water is still. The world is not a toy, a cartoon, a poster, or a prop or costume of anything physical, and it is never light-only.
keyCharacteristics: One indigo ink family in `light-dark()` pairs; a vermilion seal for a rejection or a stopped sync, and nothing else.
Recessed water (18 px corners, an inset shade) against a still margin of 1 px hairlines; no cards.
Commissioner by weight (300 titles, 400 body, 500 labels and controls, 600 emphasis); Spline Sans Mono for ids, versions and counts.
Labels in small capitals tracked 0.18em; the app's name alone at 0.32em.
Every state has a form and a word: rings, solid and dashed edges, and the state's own name.
Motion is 200 ms colour and edge changes plus 900 ms settles (a basin's change, newly lit code, a then-and-now morph); reduced motion cuts them all.

A figure keeps its words and controls in its left third and gives the stage the rest: the server's basin and list, a 5rem band of straight hairline wires, then the devices in a row. Given code, from 80rem it sets its words and playback in a band across the top and its code in a sticky column beside the stage.
Code in Spline Sans Mono at 0.8125rem, one ink in three tonal steps, wrapping at its measure on one shared edge; the branch that last ran washed in water behind a 1 px ink rule.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Every colour but the seal is a value of one indigo ink diluted toward water. A new colour joins that family or does not join; there is no second accent hue.

rules.name: The Seal Rule
rules.body: Vermilion marks a rejection and a stopped sync and nothing else. Offline, retrying, remove, hover, breaking controls, a lost message, a stopped figure and errors of form never take it.

rules.name: The Paired Value Rule
rules.body: Every colour is a `light-dark()` pair declared in `tokens.css` and mirrored in `palette.ts`, and `tokens.test.ts` holds it: text at 4.5:1 and control edges at 3:1, on page and on water, day and night. The exceptions are shadow and scrim colours, which are literal `light-dark()` rgb pairs written where they are used (see Elevation & Depth), and the system colours of forced-colours mode.

rules.name: The Tonal Syntax Rule
rules.body: Code takes no hue of its own. Shiki's CSS-variables theme names the `--code-*` aliases in `tokens.css`, and they point at three text tones, not new colours: names, constants, parameters and code's own foreground in `--text`; keywords, strings and links in `--text-2`; comments and punctuation, receding furthest, in `--text-3`. Inserted, deleted and changed text stay `--text`; fresh ink and the seal never colour code.

rules.name: The Weight Ladder Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is weight before size: 300 titles, 400 body, 500 labels and controls, 600 emphasis. Nothing is heavier than 600.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Spline Sans Mono sets ids, versions, counts and file paths, the short state lines built on them, and code, and nothing else. The state's word beside an id goes back to Commissioner (a row's "pending", the outbox's "acked"), as do the words of a choice (Then, Now), a date ("28 Sep 2026") and every sentence. Commissioner has no tabular figures, so anything that must align is mono.

rules.name: The Small Capitals Rule
rules.body: A label that names a control, a category or a device is uppercase small text tracked 0.18em; the app's name alone takes 0.32em. Small capitals never sit as a kicker or eyebrow above a title or a section, and never set a sentence.

rules.name: The Fixed Box Rule
rules.body: A row's sync state changes form inside a fixed 4.5rem slot. No state adds or removes height or width, so the list never reflows when a change lands.

rules.name: The List Leads Rule
rules.body: The list is real text on the still margin and comes first; a basin vouches for it and never replaces it or pushes it below the fold. In the app the basin is a 92 px badge beside the name.

rules.name: The Thumb Reach Rule
rules.body: Below 45rem the add form docks at the foot with the item field and Add on its first line; the DOM keeps keyboard order (item, quantity, unit, category, Add) whatever the grid shows.

rules.name: The Play First Rule
rules.body: Play or Pause is a figure's first focusable control at every width, so a world that started on its own stops at once; speed and "Your turn" follow the stage in reading order wherever the grid sets them.

rules.name: The Compact Read Rule
rules.body: A list nothing on which is a target sets its rows at 2rem (`--row-height-compact`) and its groups closer; the server's list in a figure, given room for two 10rem columns, also flows its groups in two, and a device's list keeps one. A list that takes a check or a remove keeps 2.875rem rows and its 44 px targets. In a figure the server's list is always compact, and a device's list is compact while a scene plays and regular in free play.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Code wraps at its block's measure and never scrolls sideways, every line hanging from its own indentation. The one drawing that cannot hang, Then and Now's morph (one flat run of tokens), shows only from a 40rem panel; a narrower panel cuts between per-line versions instead.

rules.name: The One Code Edge Rule
rules.body: Every code block sets its text `--space-3` in from its head and its rule. Lit code's 1 px rule takes its pixel out of the line's inset (`--lit-rule`), so lighting a span never moves a character.

rules.name: The Recessed Water Rule
rules.body: Water sits below the margin, never above it: a basin takes the inset shade and a hairline ring, never a drop shadow. Under forced colours the shade goes and a 1 px CanvasText edge keeps the water's shape.

rules.name: The Two Risers Rule
rules.body: Only the docked form and the dialog cast a shadow. Rows, buttons, fields, bands, panes, badges, code blocks and a figure's stage and wires are flat.

rules.name: The Ring Rule
rules.body: A change's state is a ring beside its id: hollow while pending, left half filled once acked, dashed in the seal when rejected, gone when synced. The row and the outbox strip draw the same ring.

rules.name: The Straight Wire Rule
rules.body: Each device has one straight hairline wire, from under the server's basin (its foot, or its list's where that runs lower) to the top of its pane. Requests ride one side of it and replies the other, every message with its label, and no message comes within 12 px of the pane, so no label sits on its header; the band is drawn over the stage, hidden from assistive technology and never a target, so it shows nothing the lists and the caption do not also say.

dos: Do take every ground, text, edge and ink colour from the thirteen custom properties in `src/styles/tokens.css`, and add any new one as a `light-dark()` pair mirrored in `src/ui/palette.ts` and checked in `tokens.test.ts` (4.5:1 text, 3:1 control edges, on page and water, day and night).

Do take spacing, corners and sizes from the tokens (`--space-1` to `--space-7`, `--radius-control`, `--radius-badge`, `--radius-basin`, `--target`, `--row-height`, `--row-height-compact`, `--rule`, `--column`), and type sizes from `--text-xs` to `--text-2xl`, `--text-2xl-phone` and, for code alone, `--text-code`.

Do give every state its form and its word: pending a hollow ring with its `#id`; acked a half-filled ring; synced no marker; rejected a dashed seal ring with the server's reason; offline a solid band; retrying a dashed band; stopped the solid band with its word in the seal, its reason and Retry.
Do keep every target at 2.75rem or more, extending a hit area with a pseudo-element where the visible shape is smaller (the badge).

Do keep state changes to colour and edge over 200 ms with `--ease-out`, and every basin change, newly lit code and a then-and-now morph to the 900 ms settle; let reduced motion, the CPU path and a figure's jumps show changes at once.
Do keep Play or Pause the first focusable control of every figure, and its breaking controls set apart from playback by space.
Do set a list nothing on which is a target at the compact density, and any list that takes a check or a remove at the regular one.
Do give every message on a wire its label, requests and replies on opposite sides of it, and a push's dot in fresh ink.

Do give forced colours their own treatment: a basin draws in system colours (water Canvas, inks CanvasText, fresh ink Highlight) inside a CanvasText edge, a wire band in CanvasText with a push in Highlight, and the rings, the checked circle and the scrub bar's track, dot and ticks keep their fills with `forced-color-adjust: none` in CanvasText (the scrub bar GrayText while it waits).
Do set ids, versions, counts, file paths, the short state lines built on them and code in Spline Sans Mono, and everything else in Commissioner.
Do colour code only through the `--code-*` aliases in `tokens.css`: names in `--text`, keywords and strings in `--text-2`, comments and punctuation in `--text-3`.
Do wrap code at its block's measure with each line hanging from its own indentation, and keep every code block's text on one edge, `--space-3` in from its head and its rule.
Do light only the span of the latest trace event a figure's lights answer, washed in `--water` behind a 1 px `--ink-2` rule, and scroll only the code to it, snapped to a whole line.
donts: Don't use the vermilion seal for anything but a rejection or a stopped sync: not offline, not retrying, not remove, not a breaking control, not hover, not a lost message, not a stopped figure.
Don't let colour or an edge pattern carry a state alone; the state's word is always there.
Don't simulate or randomise a basin, or put marbling anywhere but inside one; every pattern on the page is computed from a device's rows, and controls and grounds stay plain.
Don't box list content in cards or put fills behind rows; rows sit on the still margin between hairlines.
Don't cast a shadow from anything but the docked form and the dialog, or write a shadow colour that is not a `light-dark()` pair.
Don't change a row's box when its state changes.
Don't set prose, controls or a state's word in mono, or a number that must align in Commissioner.
Don't set any text heavier than 600, or use small capitals as a kicker or eyebrow above a title or a section.
Don't ship a value for one theme only; day and night are both designed.
